My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have Alicia Olatuja for us, for the Fillius Jazz Archive. Welcome to Hamilton.

items.title: Alicia Olatuja interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 9, 2018
items.q: I was just talking to Miles in the band about this today

ctx.x: They have to play in tune.

They have to play. MW: I wanted to ask this question. As you go through your singing career, sometimes without even making a obvious attempt to do it, your music takes on a certain cultural significance. And I wanted to ask you if you have a song in your repertoire that you think already fits this or will you have an aha moment when that moment comes? For instance. It’s 1963 and Sam Cooke sings “A Change is Gonna’ Come.” It may as well be an African-American national anthem.

Right. MW: You know what I’m saying? Everybody knows it. So I was coaching a girl, she was 17 years old, she was singing for an NAACP convention. And me and another one of the coaches said, and it was all going to be older black people. And we said if you sing this song right there won’t be a dry eye in the auditorium. And she rocked the house. So at that moment she absorbed the history of that song. It transferred into her. She realized she wasn’t just singing a melody. You know what I mean? Do you already have…
